transcript.text:
“Not working” can mean anything from a door not fully latching or a programme setting, through to a blocked filter causing a safety cut-out, or a motor/heater/control fault. The quickest way forward is to establish what it does when started. 1. Check the plug, socket switch and any fuse/consumer-unit breaker first. If the display is completely dead, try another known-working appliance in the socket if safe to do so. That separates a supply issue from a dryer fault.
2. Empty the water container if it has one, shut the door firmly, and try a normal timed or cotton programme rather than cool air/refresh. A full tank or door-latch issue can stop it starting.
3. With it switched off and unplugged, clean the lint filter. If it is a condenser or heat-pump dryer, clean the accessible lower filter/condenser area as the handbook directs. Heavy fluff restriction can make a dryer stop heating or cut out. When you select a normal drying programme and press Start, does anything happen at all—display/lights, a click, drum turning, or does it stay completely dead?
Lights come on but nothing happens when I press start. No sound, drum doesn't turn. Plug and socket are fine.

A snapped belt is less likely: normally you would still hear the motor running. The main possibilities are that the door latch/interlock or start-control circuit is not authorising the cycle, or—less commonly—that the drum is too stiff for the drive to start. 1. Switch off and unplug it, empty the drum, then turn the drum slowly by hand. Tell me whether it turns smoothly, feels stiff/grinding, or is almost stuck. A stiff drum points towards rollers/bearings or an obstruction rather than the motor itself.
2. Close the door firmly and check whether it latches with a positive click and stays shut. If it does not, the door interlock is a strong suspect and will usually need an engineer or competent repairer to diagnose/replace. If the drum turns freely and the door latches properly but pressing Start remains totally silent, the likely fault moves to the door interlock wiring, start/control circuit, or motor control. That needs internal electrical diagnosis rather than buying a motor on guesswork.

Door doesn't click shut, it swings back slightly open. The plastic tongue on the door has snapped off, found the piece on the floor. If I hold the door firmly shut and press start it runs, stops when I let go.

The broken plastic door tongue/catch is the cause. Holding the door shut lets it operate, so the dryer is recognising the door as closed; that makes a motor or control fault very unlikely. Do not keep using it while holding the door shut, or try to tape, wedge or bypass the switch—the door needs to latch securely. 1. Switch off and unplug the dryer.
2. Check the receiving slot in the dryer front: remove any loose broken plastic or fluff only; do not poke into or dismantle the switch area. If the receiver is intact, the likely repair is the door handle/catch assembly rather than the electrical door switch. If the receiver is cracked, loose, or the new catch would not line up, it may also need a door-switch/catch housing repair, which is better assessed by an engineer. The make and full model number from the rating label will be needed before identifying the correct door part.
ok, the dryer's a Hotpoint. I can read the model number inside the door recess if you need it - do you want me to?

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
Yes, please send the full model number. The broken door tongue/catch is the likely repair, and the model number is needed to identify the correct matching door handle/catch assembly. It is usually on a sticker inside the door opening or recess. If you cannot get to the label easily at the moment, that can wait. Keep the dryer unplugged and avoid using it until the door latches securely.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I don't actually know the model number offhand, I'd need to go and read it off the sticker. Give me a minute and I'll check.

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
The fault is still most clearly the broken door catch/handle: the dryer runs only while the door is physically held shut, so it is not a motor or supply fault. When you have the label, send the full model number exactly as printed. It is usually on a sticker inside the door opening/recess. That will let us narrow down the correct matching door handle/catch assembly. If the label cannot be reached right now, it can wait. Keep the dryer unplugged and do not use it unless the door latches securely; do not tape, wedge or bypass the door switch.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok, I'm not sure what it is yet, I haven't read it. Is there anything else you need from me while I look?

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
Nothing else essential at this stage. The snapped door tongue is the clear cause: the dryer runs while the door is held closed, so it needs the correct replacement door handle/catch assembly rather than investigation of the motor or electrics. While you are at the door, with the dryer unplugged, you can have a quick look at the receiving slot for any loose broken plastic or fluff. Only clear material that is plainly loose—do not poke into or dismantle the switch area. If the receiver looks cracked, loose or badly misaligned, that may need an engineer as well. The useful next detail is the full model number, usually on the sticker inside the door opening/recess. If you cannot get to it just now, it can wait.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
